<entry id="A01406">
<head-word>אִיסּוּר, </head-word>
<hw-number>II</hw-number>
<head-word>אִסּוּר</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (אסר; cmp. b. h. אֵסוּר, a. אֵיסוּר) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>band, chain;</italic> trnsf. 
<italic>social circle</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Succ. 45
<sup>b</sup> (ref. to Ps. CXVIII, 27) כל העושה א' לחג וכ' he who creates a circle for the festival with eating and drinking, i.e. social pleasures. [Oth. explan.: he who makes an 
<italic>addition</italic> to the number of festive days;—hence the popular name of אסרו חג for the day following the festivals.]</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>prohibition, interdict;</italic> also 
<italic>the forbidden object</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Ber. I, 3
<sup>b</sup> bot. דברי תורה יש בהן א' וכ' the Biblical law contains prohibitions and permissions.—א' ערוה 
<italic>an obstacle to marriage by the existing laws of incest</italic>, e.g. a man prevented from performing a levirate marriage because his late brother’s wife is his own wife’s sister; &c.—א' מצוה 
<italic>a marriage</italic> (or sexual connection) 
<italic>permitted in the Torah but forbidden by Rabbinical enactment;</italic>—so called because obedience to the Rabbis is a meritorious act (מצוה); א' קדושה 
<italic>marriage restrictions</italic> incumbent 
<italic>on priests</italic> on account of their sacred office; (another opinion inverts the last two definitions). Yeb. II, 3 (20
<sup>a</sup>).—אין א' חל על א' one prohibition can take no legal hold where another prohibition already exists; i.e. you can punish, or impose sacrificial expiation, only for the first one; e.g. if you eat the meat of an unclean animal which, besides, has not been slaughtered according to ritual (נבלה). Ib. 13
<sup>b</sup>; a. fr.—Exceptions to this principle (adopted by most authorities) are when the acceding act is: 1) א' כֹּולֵל 
<italic>a more comprehensive prohibition</italic>, i.e. 
<italic>having a wider range of prohibited objects</italic>; e.g. the law imposing abstinence from food on the Day of Atonement includes food in general, i.e. food otherwise allowed as well as food forbidden at all times; א' מֹוסִיף 
<italic>a more extensive prohibition</italic>, i.e. 
<italic>having a wider range of persons concerned;</italic> e.g. the sister of A’s wife is forbidden to him (אחות אשתו) but not to his brothers. If, afterwards, his brother B. marries that sister of A.’s wife, she is forbidden in marriage (after B.’s death) to 
<italic>all</italic> the brothers as a brother’s wife, and to A. both as his own living wife’s sister and as his late brother’s wife (אשת אח);</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition> א' בַּת אַחַת 
<italic>a coincidental prohibition</italic>, i.e. two prohibitions 
<italic>taking effect at the same moment</italic>, e.g. the Day 
<pgbrk id="pg54" />of Atonement coinciding with the Sabbath day, in which case the restrictions connected with each take effect at the same time (night-fall); </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>4)</number>
<definition> א' חָמוּר 
<italic>a heavier prohibition</italic>, i.e. a prohibition 
<italic>imposing larger restrictions</italic>, e.g. the law prohibiting 
<italic>any</italic> profitable use of thing (א' הנאה), compared to the lighter prohibition, א' קַל, not to eat or drink a thing (v. infra).</definition>
<notes> Yeb. 32
<sup>b</sup> sq; Shebu. 24
<sup>ab</sup>; Ḥull. 101
<sup>a</sup> sq; Kerith. 14
<sup>b</sup>.—א' תורה 
<italic>a Biblical prohibitory law;</italic> א' דרבנן 
<italic>a Rabbinical prohibitory enactment</italic>.—א' לאו 
<italic>a prohibition expressed in the Law by a plain</italic> (לֹא) ‘thou shalt not’, without defining the penalty, in which case the latter consists of thirty nine lashes (v. מַלְקוּת).—א' כרת 
<italic>a prohibition to which the Bible attaches the penalty of excision</italic> (by the hand of God).—א' מיתה a prohibition the transgression of which the Bible punishes with death (execution).—א' אכילה 
<italic>the law not to eat</italic> (meat boiled with milk); א' הנאה 
<italic>not to make any use</italic> (of it, as selling &c.); א' בישול 
<italic>not to boil</italic> (meat with milk). Ḥull. 115
<sup>b</sup>; a. fr.—א' במות, v. בָּמָה.—
<plural-form>Pl. אִיסּוּרִין</plural-form>. Ḥull. 98
<sup>a</sup> sq. כל א' שבתורה (בטלין) בששים all things Biblically forbidden are neutralized if mixed with a quantity sixty times as large; ib. במאה—in a quantity one hundred times as large; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<senses>
<sense>
<definition> [also ָה, a. with one ו]
<pos> m.</pos> (Ispe. noun of סב, סבב = h. אִיסְטֵיב q. v., b. h. מֵסֵב; v. אִיסְ־) 
<italic>a surrounding, attachment</italic>, whence </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>balcony, colonnade, portico</italic>
<alternative>(also 
<italic>an independent colonnade</italic>)</alternative>, esp. הָאִ' the Itst’ba (Ist’ba) 
<italic>the Temple portico</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Pes. I, 5 (11
<sup>b</sup>) על גג האיצ' Ms. M. (Bab. ed. incorr. גב, Var. אִסְטְוָה, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note). Ib. 13
<sup>b</sup> one recited על גב on top (inside) …, say על גג הא' on the roof of the Its. (so as to expose it to public view). Y. Sabb. I, 2
<sup>d</sup> bot. איסטוה וכ'; Bab. 7
<sup>a</sup> איצ' שלפני העמודים a balcony in front of the columns (projecting into the street, used as a stand for dealers, v. אִיסְטֵיב). Ib. דוקא א' דלא ניחא תשמישיה Ms. M. (ed. א' הוא דלא) only the colonnade the use of which for passers by is not convenient. Num. R. s. 12 two columns of silver which were placed in front of the Ark כמין איסטווה (Cant. R. to I, 11 אִיסְטְוִוין pl.) forming a kind of balcony; Y. Sot. VIII, 22
<sup>c</sup> תנם לא' allow the surplus of three handbreadths (over the space occupied by the Tablets) for the balcony.—Yoma 49
<sup>a</sup> דעבוד מעשה אסטווה Ar. (ed. איצ') they (the laymen) served only the purpose of a portico (holding the bowls up to view, v. Pes. I, 5, but not handing them to the altar).—Y. Succ. V, 55
<sup>a</sup> bot., v. דִּיפְּלֵי.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> (cmp. הֶסֵּב, הֲסִיבָּה) 
<italic>something to recline on; couch, seat</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Kid. 70
<sup>a</sup>, (to one using the high-toned קרפיטא q. v.) א' דאמרי אינשי call it itst’ba as the people do.—M. Kat. 10
<sup>b</sup> למבני א' Ar. a. ed. (Var. as Yoma l. c.) to build a temporary 
<italic>banqueting place</italic> for guests during the festive week, cmp. אַכְוַרְנְקָא, (Rashi: 
<italic>stone building</italic>, Ms. Rashi כסא).—
<plural-form>Pl. אִיצְטְבָאֹות</plural-form> (h. form). Ex. R. s. 31 (basilicas).—אִיצְטְבֵי (Chald. form). Pes. 65
<sup>b</sup> דמסגי אא' they (the priests) walked alongside the walls on balconies (projecting boards made for them that they should not tread on the blood); Y. ib. V, 32
<sup>c</sup> bot. מִסְטְוָיֹות, V. מִסְטְוָה.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<definition>
<italic>squeezing, pressure</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Yeb. 121
<sup>b</sup> top, אגב איצצא מזקי (Ar. איצא) on account of the pressure (which the falling person exercises on the serpents in the pit) they injure him. Sabb. 144
<sup>b</sup> דאתי בתר איצצא Ar. (ed. איצצתא; Ms. M. אִיצִיצָא) (the juice) which oozes out of the grapes through the pressure of their non weight. M. Kat. 11

<plural-form>Pl. אִיצְצֵי</plural-form>. Ib. שיתין א' sixty times pressed and washed.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition> trnsf. 
<italic>depression, depreciation</italic> in the market; [oth.</definition>
<notes> opin. 
<italic>deterioration</italic> of quality]. Keth. 100
<sup>b</sup> אע"ג דנפל ביה איצצתא (read דנפלא; Ar. דהוי ביה איצא, Rashi איצצא) though there is a risk 
<italic>of depreciation</italic> (on account of large supply for the festive season) [or 
<italic>of getting sour</italic>].</notes></sense></senses></entry>
